chunks: This [is it]; let them taste it: boiling water and cold, clammy, fetid drink.

key_terms.حَمِيمٌ: Boiling water or scalding fluid used as a drink for the inhabitants of Hell.
key_terms.غَسَّاقٌ: A cold, clammy, fetid discharge or fluid from the intestines of the inhabitants of Hell.
key_terms.فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ: So let them taste it (imperative, referring to the punishment).

ai.seo_question: What are Hamim and Ghasaq in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Sad highlights the dual nature of Hell's torment, where 'Hamim' (boiling water) and 'Ghasaq' (a cold, foul drink) represent both physical agony and spiritual disgust for those who rejected Imam Ali's (AS) authority. This sensory punishment serves as a direct consequence of their arrogance and failure to recognize divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt.
